questions.stem: The SI unit of power is the
questions.explanation: Power is work done per unit time, so its unit is the joule per second, which is given the special name watt. One watt equals one joule per second.

distractorRationale.a: The joule measures work or energy, not the rate at which it is transferred
distractorRationale.d: The kilowatt-hour is a practical unit of energy used for electricity bills, not a unit of power

questions.stem: Two labourers carry identical loads up the same staircase. The first takes 10 minutes and the second takes 30 minutes. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The first does three times as much work
The second does three times as much work
They do the same work, but the first develops three times the power
They do the same work and develop the same power

questions.explanation: Work done against gravity is mgh, which depends only on the load and the height, so it is the same for both. Power is work divided by time, so completing the same work in a third of the time means three times the power.

distractorRationale.a: Work does not depend on how quickly it is done
distractorRationale.b: Taking longer does not increase the work done; it reduces the power
distractorRationale.d: The work is indeed equal, but the times differ so the powers cannot be equal

questions.stem: A machine does 6000 J of work in 30 s. Calculate its power. Give your answer in watts.
questions.explanation: $P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{6000}{30} = 200\ \text{W}$. Since 1 W = 1 J/s, dividing joules by seconds gives watts directly.

questions.stem: A crane lifts a load of mass 500 kg through a vertical height of 12 m in 20 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the useful power developed. Give your answer in watts.
questions.explanation: Useful work $= mgh = 500 \times 10 \times 12 = 60\,000\ \text{J}$. Power $= \frac{60\,000}{20} = 3000\ \text{W}$, that is 3.0 kW.

questions.stem: A car engine exerts a steady forward force of 1500 N while the car travels at a constant 20 m/s. Calculate the power developed by the engine. Give your answer in watts.
questions.explanation: For motion at constant speed, $P = Fv = 1500 \times 20 = 30\,000\ \text{W}$, that is 30 kW. Because the speed is constant, this driving force exactly balances the total resistance to motion.

questions.stem: The efficiency of a machine is given by

options.text: total energy input ÷ useful energy output × 100 %
useful energy output ÷ total energy input × 100 %
useful energy output × total energy input × 100 %

questions.explanation: Efficiency asks what fraction of what you supplied comes out as something useful, so the useful output must be on top. Because output can never exceed input, this definition also guarantees efficiency is never more than 100 %.

distractorRationale.a: Inverted, so it would always give a value greater than 100 % — a clear signal the fraction is upside down
distractorRationale.c: Multiplying gives a quantity with units of energy squared, which is meaningless as a ratio
distractorRationale.d: This compares the waste with the useful output, which is a different ratio altogether

questions.stem: A machine is supplied with 800 J of energy and delivers 600 J of useful work. Calculate its efficiency. Give your answer as a percentage.
questions.explanation: Efficiency $= \frac{600}{800} \times 100 = 75\%$. The remaining 200 J, that is 25 % of the input, is wasted mainly as heat through friction.

questions.stem: No practical machine has an efficiency of 100 % mainly because

options.text: energy is destroyed inside the machine
some input energy is converted into heat and sound by friction
the output force is always smaller than the input force

questions.explanation: Energy is always conserved, so the input energy is never lost — but part of it is converted into forms that are not useful for the job, chiefly heat generated by friction and sound. Only the remainder appears as useful output, so efficiency falls below 100 %.

distractorRationale.a: Energy cannot be destroyed; the principle of conservation of energy forbids it
distractorRationale.c: Even a perfectly operated machine has friction, so poor use is not the fundamental reason
distractorRationale.d: Many machines multiply force; the shortfall is in energy, not in force

questions.stem: A pump rated 2500 W raises 300 kg of water through a height of 15 m in 30 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the efficiency of the pump. Give your answer as a percentage.
questions.explanation: Useful work $= mgh = 300 \times 10 \times 15 = 45\,000\ \text{J}$. Useful output power $= \frac{45\,000}{30} = 1500\ \text{W}$. Efficiency $= \frac{1500}{2500} \times 100 = 60\%$. Both quantities must be powers before dividing — comparing 45 000 J with 2500 W would be meaningless.

questions.stem: A student of mass 50 kg runs up a flight of stairs of vertical height 5.0 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the useful power he develops against gravity. Give your answer in watts.
questions.explanation: Work done against gravity $= mgh = 50 \times 10 \times 5.0 = 2500\ \text{J}$. Power $= \frac{2500}{10} = 250\ \text{W}$. Only the vertical height counts, so the length of the staircase along the slope is irrelevant.
